scenes.say: Star or snowflake schema? Which one do you pick for analytics? Let’s break it down.
A star schema has a central fact table linked to denormalized dimensions. It’s fast and simple. Snowflake schema splits dimensions into related tables, reducing redundancy but adding joins.

scenes.label: Star
scenes.sub: Sales_Fact links to Customer_Dim with all info
scenes.say: For example, in a star schema, your Sales Fact table links straight to a Customer Dimension packed with all customer info.
With snowflake, Customer Dimension connects to a separate Geography table for location. More tables, but less repeated data.

scenes.question: Is snowflake always better for big data?
scenes.right: Not always. Only normalize if dimensions are huge or hierarchical. Star is usually faster for analytics.
scenes.say: Don’t fall for this: Snowflake isn’t always better for big data. Only normalize if your dimensions are huge or have hierarchies. Star schemas are usually faster for analytics.
